newsitem.title: USA: Cargill crushing plant down, others said to slow.
newsitem.headline: Cargill crushing plant down, others said to slow.

text.p: A Cargill Inc -owned crushing facility in Guntersville, Ala. will take downtime from March 12 through the 27, a Cargill official confirmed.
Flooding in the Ohio River Valley had made it difficult for the Guntersville facility to secure soybeans, so previously scheduled downtime will be taken early, the official said.
"The downtime is a blessing in disguise for them because the (crushing) margins have been so bad," a dealer said.
The soybean market's recent stretch to multi-year highs have depressed crushing margins and generated widespread talk that soymeal and soyoil production would slow this week.
"Margins have deteriorated a lot and that will pressure the pace of the crush," said one Indiana-based crusher.
"As margins dictate, we will slow our crush," he said.
The trade had been anticipating a slowdown in the pace of the crush beginning this month.
However last week's National Oilseed Processor's Association weekly crushing pace of 30.078 million bushels still hovered around historically high levels.
In its latest supply and demand forecast, the U.S. Department of Agriculture raised the 1996-97 U.S. crush to a record high 1.420 billion bushels, up 10 million bushels from its previous forecast.
One Kansas City-based dealer said that the crush was likely to be strong again this week because some crushers still have large inventories of soybeans to work through.
"They are going to talk about a slowdown, but until you see it actually happen, don't believe it," the dealer said.
